If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testLargeSample()` of `PolynomialFitterTest` attempts to fit polynomial functions of degrees 0 to 9 on very large samples (40,000 points) generated with noise. The current bug report indicates an issue in the usage of large weight vectors in multivariate vector optimizers, whereby a full nxn weight matrix is created unnecessarily when passing a vector of weights. This causes excessive memory consumption and potential crashes when the number of points is large.

The test uses `PolynomialFitter.fit(double[])` to fit the polynomial, which internally calls `fit(new PolynomialFunction.Parametric(), guess)` (line 68). Attempts to inspect deeper `fit` overloads resulted in seeing only the forwarding methods, but it is understood that the fitting operation likely calls multivariate vector optimizers with weights. Because the number of data points in the test is 40,000, a large weight array would cause the optimizer to create a huge weight matrix internally.

Thus, the root cause appears to be that the multivariate vector optimizer or the fitter passes the weights inefficiently as a vector, leading to the creation and copying of a full nxn matrix for weights. This excessively uses memory with large sample sizes and results in failure in the test or memory exhaustion.

No recent bug reports directly relate to this weight matrix issue or the polynomial fitter. The test reproduces the bug by fitting with a large number of points. This explains why the test fails only when sample size is large.

In summary:
- The `PolynomialFitter` uses `LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer` optimizer.
- The optimizer, when receiving large vector weights, creates full n by n matrix internally.
- This causes memory exhaustion when sample size (number of weights) is large.
- The test triggers this by fitting polynomial on 40,000 points.
- Fix would require optimizing how weights are passed to the optimizer, avoiding constructing dense full matrices from weight vectors.

Next steps should be to inspect the code in `PolynomialFitter` and optimizer to confirm how weights are passed and handled, and make them efficient for large samples.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
